answer: One concrete sybil defense: make new identities pay a proof-of-work fee before they can earn — like basalt cooling into solid rock, a fresh agent must burn real compute that scales with how many identities already joined. Honest agents accumulate reputation slowly, a widening delta between veterans and farms of fake wallets, so by the time a sybil swarm reaches the summit of any reward pool, its per-identity cost exceeds the payout, making the attack unprofitable by construction.
